panels.title: Gateway request rate by status class
panels.description: api-gateway http_requests_total grouped by status family. 2xx/3xx = served; 4xx incl. the 429 rate-limit hits; 5xx/502 = upstream failures (e.g. a downed service — see chaos case 4).

panels.title: Rate-limit hits (429/s) at the edge
panels.description: rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status="429"}). The ceiling sweep (RESULTS.md) showed a single client IP knees at ~10 req/s (auth tier) and ~50 req/s (api tier) → these are the per-IP fixed-window limits. Sustained >5/s for 10m fires GatewayRateLimitSurge.

panels.title: Gateway p99 latency
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.99) over the gateway's own http_request_duration_seconds. This is edge-observed latency (proxy + upstream round-trip).

panels.title: Top edge routes by request rate
panels.description: sum by (route) of the gateway's request rate — which public paths carry the traffic. Routes are the post-/v1 templates (e.g. /{*path} for the catch-all proxy).

options.content:
**Edge capacity (measured — tests/load/RESULTS.md).** From a SINGLE client IP the per-IP rate limit is the first ceiling: **auth ~10 req/s**, **general API ~50 req/s** (excess → 429, by design, brute-force/abuse protection — NOT a backend failure). True backend ceilings (rate-limit bypassed, direct-to-service): login ~30/s (Argon2 CPU cliff), discovery ~100/s (fan-out+replica), booking ≥100/s, GPS-WS ≥800 concurrent (0 conn failures).

**Gap — active WS sessions:** the gateway/presence do not export a live WS-session gauge today, so there is no edge-WS-sessions panel. The WS ceiling is characterised by the load suite (`ceiling-ws.js`) instead. Exporting a `ws_active_connections` gauge is a tracked follow-up.
